idiom_name: Akka typed actor: Behaviors.receive handler invoked by the dispatcher from the mailbox
implementation_notes: In Scala the classic listener object collapses into an actor: Behaviors.receive declares the handler, ActorRef.tell/! enqueues the message in the mailbox, and the dispatcher invokes the behavior when it processes the mailbox - the consumer holds no thread between messages, and an actor instance processes one message at a time, so no locks are needed. What replaces the classic structure is the mailbox-plus-behavior pair (the carrier library is Akka/Pekko); stream integrations express the same inversion as a Sink, and a Java-style MessageListener is implemented directly only when a Java messaging client demands its listener interface.
pitfalls: Mailboxes are unbounded by default and delivery is at-most-once: bound the mailbox and add persistence/retry when a crash must not lose messages.
A blocking handler stalls the dispatcher thread shared with many other actors; use a dedicated dispatcher or offload the blocking work.
tell/! is fire-and-forget with no back-pressure signal; use ask or streams when the producer must be slowed down.
